candidates.tagline: Only 10% of buyers want a fully driverless car — Musk just announced one for Tesla's bestselling family SUV anyway
candidates.story: At the NY Times DealBook Summit on November 19, 2026, Elon Musk announced Tesla will build a Model Y variant with no steering wheel or pedals — despite Tesla's own robotaxi fleet already using steering-wheel-equipped Model Ys, and Cox Automotive finding only 10% of US consumers prefer fully driverless Level 5 autonomy (down from 17% in 2016); Musk gave no timeline, price, or location.
candidates.why_funny: Tesla's solution to low demand for autonomous cars is to remove the steering wheel from the car most people buy for its practicality, then announce it at a conference with zero concrete details about when or how it would ever work.
candidates.alt: Tesla vehicle interior showing the driver's seat and dashboard with no steering wheel installed — a demonstration of the wheel-free design Musk announced for a Model Y variant

candidates.tagline: The $999 gaming chair that rattles your spine on every explosion — because apparently a monitor wasn't immersive enough
candidates.story: On November 13, 2026, Razer launched the Soma Pro — a $999 gaming chair with six built-in Sensa HD haptic motors that vibrate your whole body in sync with in-game explosions and impacts, plus THX Spatial Audio speakers mounted in the chair back; Gizmodo headlined their review 'Rattles Your Spine and Blasts Your Ears in Pursuit of Immersion.'
candidates.why_funny: Razer's answer to the question 'how do we make gaming more immersive?' was: physically assault the gamer from the chair itself, then charge a thousand dollars for the privilege.
candidates.alt: Razer Soma Pro gaming chair with RGB lighting, showing the chair's design with built-in haptic motors and speakers mounted in the headrest and back — the $999 chair that vibrates in sync with game events
